title: Industrial X-Ray — the pre-visit copilot (2-minute demo)

voice.instructions: Calm, confident, warm product-demo narrator. Clear international English, steady moderate pace, short natural pauses between sentences.

lines.text: When a technician is sent to an unfamiliar plant, the first visit is where the time goes.
Finding the equipment, understanding the fault, clearing access and reaching an expert all happen on site, under pressure.
Industrial X-Ray turns a scan of the site into a workspace you can prepare in before you travel.
This is Valmet's equipment room: 1.7 million Gaussian splats, split into 676 object candidates and linked to maintenance records.
And we show honestly how many of those are confidently identified.
A technician is preparing to service pump P-005. They ask where it is, and the copilot takes them there.
The likely fault is fouling, with 52 percent confidence, and every claim links to its source record.
A pallet truck blocks the service area. In Plan mode they move a virtual stand-in, and collisions, clearance and the route update at once. The scan itself never changes.
The inspection robot checks a collision-free way in.
X-Ray opens the pump, with the suspect parts in red, ready for a short scored practice run.
Finally, they pin a question on the scene and send the whole context to a remote expert, who replies with a recommendation and a draft work order.
For Valmet, that means technicians who arrive prepared: faster equipment identification, access planned in advance, and more useful remote support, in a browser with nothing to install.
The asset data here is synthetic and the savings are not yet measured. A pilot would measure time to find equipment and time to prepare a visit.
Industrial X-Ray. Know the site before you set foot in it.
